gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-libertinus-serif: Loud, ruler-straight lettering from Happy Monkey sits over Libertinus Serif, a text serif whose bowls swell ever so slightly. But shrink the heading and its wide-gapped e loses its swagger.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-libre-caslon-text: Bold through and through, Happy Monkey gives its bars the full weight of its stems, while Libre Caslon Text swells gently. Their disagreement is the draw: rigid line against living curve.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-lustria: A line that never swells mid-curve defines Happy Monkey, set against Lustria, whose serif letters carry the mild variation of letterpress. Longer paragraphs would read with a traditional, steady dignity.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-maitree: Fine rope laid into letter shapes gives Happy Monkey a knack for grabbing attention. Maitree, a classic serif with open-mouthed curves, is the one that settles in and carries the text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-marcellus: Pure drawn line: Happy Monkey traces each letter at constant weight, while Marcellus shifts its strokes like etched glass. One is made to announce, the other to be read closely.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-martel: Happy Monkey draws every letter with one uninterrupted line width and wide gaps in the e. Martel, a text serif, would carry paragraphs with ease, its moderate contrast and horseshoe-like openings keeping the going smooth.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mate: Happy Monkey keeps every join at full stroke weight, while Mate cups its rounds and eases from heavy to light. Rigid and soft, each makes the other easier to notice.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mate-sc: Dignified Mate SC, a text serif, carries a faint nib pressure across each round letter. And Happy Monkey, all spaghetti-like same-width strokes, is the foil that makes that softness show.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Distinctive to the last stroke, Happy Monkey draws attention with a zero-modulation line. Nanum Myeongjo, a serif with quiet modulation and open curve tips, is the one made for reading.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-noto-serif-hk: Happy Monkey draws each letter like a taut string. Noto Serif HK, a text serif, keeps its modulation faint and its curve endings generous, and that quiet is what makes the pairing work.
